A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Continuous Domain Generalization and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B. Corresponding content can be matched despite renaming, reformatting, and table renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification and forecasting experiments, descriptor-robustness tests, and appendix ablation, scalability, sensitivity, and convergence results.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical evaluations, revises benchmark results, and adds operator-consistency measurements in Section 5.4 and Table 2.

M1.justification: The transport equations, gating, local charts, losses, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged; NeuralLTO becomes NeuralLio. However, Appendix A.3 changes the reported fMoW model architecture from a three-layer convolutional backbone to pretrained ResNet-50 and changes its prediction head, a limited architectural revision.

E1.justification: The six benchmark datasets and their domain definitions remain. Appendix A.3 nevertheless revises Traffic's prediction task from six-step to three-step forecasting, narrowing the forecast target rather than adding another dataset. The removed fMoW ablation does not remove fMoW from overall evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same baseline methods and benchmark participation, including the Yearbook-only temporal comparisons. The timing comparison and ablation variant sets also remain. Appendix A.2 corrects DNA to NDA without changing the nearest-domain method.

E3.justification: Appendix A.3 replaces fMoW's backbone with ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50, changes its head dimensions and stated field-network dimension, and changes basis counts from five to two for 2-Moons and three for MNIST. Traffic changes from 12 historical inflow/outflow pairs and six-step prediction to 48 pairs and three-step prediction. Section 5.4 adds cosine-similarity protocols over self-transports, descriptor triplets, and round trips. These are reported setting changes; the PDFs do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Section 5.4 directly tests the central identity, associativity, and invertibility properties of the learned operator, adding an analytical question absent from v1. Conversely, Appendix A.5 removes the fMoW component ablations, and Figure 4 revises the extreme-incompleteness result. The scalability, sensitivity, and convergence analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five runs with different random seeds and report benchmark means and standard deviations. No revised run count, significance test, confidence interval procedure, or uncertainty estimator is introduced. New Table 2 provides point similarities without an additional uncertainty analysis.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces the fMoW results: proposed error changes from 35.9 ± 0.5% to 24.5 ± 0.5%, and the best baseline changes from CIDA at 36.7 ± 0.5% to DANN at 26.0 ± 0.7%. The changed architecture prevents interpreting this as a same-setting gain. V2 adds identity/associativity/invertibility similarities of 99.9/99.1/98.3%, removes the fMoW ablation entries, and changes Figure 4's No-Chart error at seven missing dimensions from approximately 23% to 17%. Other Table 1 columns retain their numerical values.

T1.justification: Appendix A.4 changes the definition of E in O(2(Dn + E) + F) from remaining encoder-and-decoder parameters to remaining encoder parameters, a limited revision to the complexity accounting. The central theorem, proof, and transport equations remain; the ideal, complete descriptor-space qualification is made more explicit.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: the CDG formulation, parameter-manifold foundation, Lie transport, descriptor gating, local charts, and superior generalization and robustness. The additional structural experiment supports an existing claim rather than introducing a new core contribution.

C2.justification: Sections 4.1 and 4.3 explicitly distinguish the ideal latent descriptor space from observed projections. Section 5.2 expands the geometric interpretation of the parameter surface, and new Section 5.4 interprets high cosine similarities as confirming Lie-group transport. Appendix A.9's substantive limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository link in the abstract and Appendix A.3 and revises several architecture specifications. However, it removes the explicit 500-epoch training statement and previously stated dropout rates for MNIST, fMoW, and Yearbook. These omissions do not establish that the underlying training budget or dropout settings changed.

R1.justification: The reference list is unchanged, but Section 2 revises the positioning against AdaGraph and CIDA. V1 emphasizes their domain-adaptation setting and target-data requirements; v2 instead emphasizes discrete graphs and distance-based relationships as insufficient for a global mapping over domain variation.

P1.justification: V2 polishes and expands explanations in the introduction, methodology, qualitative analysis, and conclusion; renames NeuralLTO to NeuralLio; corrects NDA terminology; and updates author and conference information. The overall narrative and main/appendix organization remain, apart from the added Section 5.4.

P2.justification: V2 adds the structural-property table, removes the fMoW ablation column, and places the narrower ablation table beside prose. Figures 2, 4, and 6 receive formatting changes, Figure 5's caption expands, and several floats move. Most underlying figures and the overall document design remain.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful structural diagnostics, clearer explanations, and code-access information. These gains coexist with removal of fMoW ablation evidence and explicit training details. Traffic's revised forecasting setup retains the old scores without explaining their correspondence, while Figure 4's diminished extreme-incompleteness advantage is not reflected in the interpretation. The PDFs therefore support identifiable benefits and losses, but not a reliable net judgment of overall improvement.
